area.title: Journey flow, step order and what applies when
area.scope: How the notification journey hangs together across pages: the version mount and session, the step order and next-page rules, the opening run, change and return contexts (from hub, from review, from template review), the shared journey buttons and their actions, the status strip and reference, the obligations and scope rules saying which questions apply to which consignment and what is optional versus a hard stop, the end-to-end journeys walked whole, the prototype's route and coverage tables, and the decisions ledger. Stops at any one page's own content. Includes the high-risk plants frontend's flow, opening run, entry guard, section captions, feature registry, obligation set index and set mount, and the rest of its decisions ledger (standing rulings, parked behaviours, non-functional rulings).

sources.role: the decision that pagination is kept everywhere and that its earlier removal was an error: every address book list and every address picker pages, and no requirement says a list of an organisation's addresses is served or shown unpaginated. It drops req-611's 'unpaginated' clause and supersedes ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 on that point alone, because that point's reasoning rested on the address book's list endpoint taking no role and so having to be read whole and paged for display, which is no longer true of the service: RequestedListFilters takes roles and searchRoles, AddressController lists one page at a time with page and pageSize, and ListPaging sets 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, exactly the bounds ruling:paul-2026-11-05 point 8 names. The role filter runs in the service before the page is cut, so paging the API cannot make it wrong, and Paul's point 8 stands in full. The rest of ruling:ian-2026-11-23 stands: the pickers page at eight, the one-page clause of inc-087's criteria 7, 8 and 9 stays dropped with req-594 and req-595, and the 'Selected address' restatement comes back with the paging. EUDPA-827 is the fix and has landed on the animals frontend's main. It settles conflict c-292 by keeping the plants contact picker's pagination and inset, and the contact picker pages at eight rather than five, confirmed by Ian the same day, so every picker in both journeys pages at the figure the INS address book list already uses and ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 1 set for the other pickers.

sources.role: the decision that the live animals and high-risk plants party pickers page at eight, and that the one-page clause of inc-087's criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped along with req-594, req-595 and the paging and inset half of c-094's outcome. The clause rested on ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-041, which that file heads as the orchestrator's application of Sam's principle rather than a ruling of Sam's: point 3b is about live filtering alone, and the bullet three lines above builds the INS address book list at 8 a page over the same records. The prototype's single page is read off a book too small to need paging, so it is evidence either way only under ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116, which keeps the prototype to look and feel rather than architecture; ruling:ian-2026-11-11 point 2 is not the ground, being scoped to app/data and data claims. Eight is the INS address book list's figure alone: the transporter list renders no pagination yet, EUDPA-824 being To Do. The 'Selected address' inset comes back with the paging, because req-595's own reason for dropping it was that one page put the chosen row always on screen. req-611 is unaffected: the address book's role-scoped list stays unpaginated, because each frontend reads the whole book to filter by role and pages what is left for display.

claims.statement: The live animals and high-risk plants party pickers show eight of a role's addresses a page.
claims.quote: The pickers page at eight, and the one-page clause of `inc-087`'s criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped.
claims.note: New. Answers the report question the bug raised against inc-087 criterion 7.

claims.statement: The one-page clause of inc-087's acceptance criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped.
claims.quote: the one-page clause of `inc-087`'s criteria 7, 8 and 9 is dropped
claims.note: New. The clause this ruling withdraws, named by criterion.

claims.statement: Eight a page is the figure the INS address book list already uses, which is why the pickers take it.
claims.quote: Eight is the figure the INS address book list already uses (`insfrontend:src/server/app/features/address-book/list/list.controller.js:49`, `REQ-INS-ADDR-013`).
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The animals transporter list is not a precedent for how many addresses a page holds, because it renders no pagination today and the ticket to split it into pages of eight is still to do.
claims.quote: The animals transporter list is **not** a precedent: it renders no pagination today, and EUDPA-824, the ticket to split it into pages of eight, is still To Do.
claims.note: New. Refuses a precedent rather than setting one.

claims.statement: Paging the pickers sits on top of the role filtering, which stays as it is.
claims.quote: Paging comes back on top of the role filtering, which is correct and stays.
claims.note: New. Leaves the role filtering inc-087 built untouched.

claims.statement: The one-page clause was a distillation error: it rests on a claim that is the orchestrator's application of Sam's principle on live filtering, not a ruling of Sam's on how many addresses a page holds.
claims.quote: **It was a distillation error, and the error is identifiable.** The clause rests on `ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-041`, which is the orchestrator's application of Sam's principle, not a ruling of Sam's on paging
claims.note: New. Names the claim the withdrawn clause rested on.

claims.statement: Sam's point 3b rules on when results refresh, not on how many addresses a page holds.
claims.quote: It rules on when results refresh, not on how many a page holds.
claims.note: New. The ground on which the earlier claim is read as not covering paging.

claims.statement: The same afternoon ruling builds the INS address book list at eight a page three lines above the sentence that removed the pickers' paging, over the same address-book records, so one page of it holds two incompatible answers, and eight is the one with a requirement behind it.
claims.quote: One ruling, one page of it, two incompatible answers to how many addresses a page holds. Eight is the one with a requirement behind it.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The prototype showing one page of addresses is a fixture of an address book too small to need paging, not a requirement that a page holds every address.
claims.quote: **The prototype's single page is a fixture, not a requirement.** `prototype-dr2-1-source-p8-063` reads one page off the prototype's own address book, which holds too few records to need paging, so the prototype could not show paging whether it wanted it or not.
claims.note: New. Sets aside the prototype claim behind the one-page clause.

claims.statement: How many rows a page holds over a real dataset that grows is not look and feel, so the prototype is not the authority for it.
claims.quote: It rests instead on `ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-116`, "Prototype is the authority for how things look and feel not how they are architected": how many rows a page holds over a real dataset that grows is not look and feel
claims.note: New. Says which earlier claim point 4 rests on, and which it does not.

claims.statement: The "Selected address: <name>" restatement comes back with the paging, between the search box and the results, in the words both frontends already had.
claims.quote: The inset goes back where it was, between the search box and the results, with the words both frontends already had.
claims.note: New. Reverses req-595's removal of the inset.

claims.statement: The reason req-595 gave for dropping the restatement no longer holds, because the chosen row can be on another page again and a trader on page two would otherwise have nothing on screen telling them what they have chosen.
claims.quote: Once the chosen row can be on another page again, that reason is gone: a trader on page two would otherwise have nothing on screen telling them what they have chosen.
claims.note: New. Why the inset returns rather than merely that it does.

claims.statement: The address book's own role-scoped list stays unpaginated: each frontend reads the whole book because the list endpoint takes no role, filters by role itself, and then pages what is left for display.
claims.quote: The address book's own role-scoped list stays unpaginated: each frontend reads the whole book because the list endpoint takes no role, filters by role itself, and then pages what is left for display. Paging the API would make the role filter wrong.
claims.note: New. Leaves req-611 as it is.

claims.statement: inc-087 stays done, because it was built as its criteria then read, and the code, the criteria, the requirements behind them, c-094's outcome and the behaviour spec are corrected under EUDPA-827 so a re-distillation does not drop paging or the restatement again.
claims.quote: **`inc-087` stays done.** It was built as its criteria then read. The code is corrected under EUDPA-827, which also corrects the criteria, the requirements behind them, `c-094`'s outcome and the behaviour spec, so a re-distillation does not drop paging or the restatement again.
claims.note: New. Says the increment is not reopened and where the correction lands.

claims.statement: The ruling does not say what the pickers offer once a search narrows a role's list to eight or fewer, so whether pagination disappears on a narrowed list is left open here.
claims.note: New. The ruling fixes the page size and the restatement but says nothing about a search narrowing the list below the threshold; the behaviour spec settles it.

sources.role: the owner's answers to the overview and review theme's engineering review: plants shows the notification task list heading visibly as live animals does, reading "Notification task list" in both services; each posting button on the notification view header gets its own form, as every other posting button in the service does, so Amend and Copy as new each post their own and Delete stays a link to the delete confirmation page outside both, in the live animals and plants frontends; tests find live animals review cards by GOV.UK structure and role rather than by the words of a numbered heading; every other atypical item the review found is fixed, except the local stack's automatic uploader restart, the plants journey spec ruling deleted rather than superseded, the tests repo's deleted docs note on why Cancel amend waits on the URL, and the animals backend unit tests that build a real DocumentService on stubbed repositories; and the fixes land in as few increments as sensible rather than one per item. It also replaces the 16 November ruling's "what stays" clause on outstanding items: the animals backend stops storing the outstanding items list and the rule that works it out comes off the OutstandingItem enum, both re-added with the future outstanding-actions banner, while the submitted date is still recorded. sources.role: the decision that the exporter clause of inc-087 acceptance criterion 2 is dropped and no EXPORTER role is to be added anywhere. The clause rested on two prototype claims reading the prototype internal consignor-or-exporter type vocabulary (app/routes.js, app/data/consignment-address-sections.js) as a domain role, which ruling:ian-2026-11-11 point 2 already bars and which ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 22 gives to the address book service as architecture rather than look and feel. What the prototype means is that one section covers both parties under the heading Consignor, which the real service already models as the single CONSIGNOR role and inc-087 already satisfies. The bar on app/data is on what the file is, not on how a claim is labelled: a rule claim from those files is refused as readily as a data one.

claims.statement: Design question 10 does not go to the designer now.
claims.quote: so the question does not go to the designer now
claims.note: Follows from the owner parking the work; the owner does not mention the designer.

claims.statement: Before a Design Release 2.1 row goes to the designer or into the build loop, someone asks whether it is needed for the deadline.

claims.note: A standing rule the main session draws from the owner's complaint that concept work is 'mixed in with the "get this done work" making things confusing'; the owner states the problem, not this rule.

claims.statement: A feature the real service's main branch does not have at all, shown only in the prototype, is the usual sign that a row is concept work.
claims.quote: a feature main does not have at all, shown only in the prototype, is the usual sign of concept work
claims.note: The test for spotting concept work is the main session's reading; the owner gives templates and address search as instances but no test.

claims.statement: A row judged to be concept work is flagged to Sam rather than built.

claims.note: Follows from the owner being the one who ruled on templates and address search; the owner does not ask to be flagged.

claims.statement: The ruling leaves open what happens to the templates work: it calls templates concept work but does not say whether templates are parked, deferred, dropped or still built for the deadline, and names no increment or requirement for them.
The ruling leaves open who picks the parked address-search work back up, when, and what would unpark it: it says only that it is not needed yet.

The country search on the live animals, germinal products and high-risk plants origin pages is the GOV.UK accessible autocomplete the real service's main branch already uses, not the prototype's hand-built search: decided item 1 says the country search 'keeps' that component's own announcements, which only holds if the component itself stays, so nothing is built to replace it.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-11-09.md claim 1, read with the context paragraph (line 15)
claims.quote: **The country search keeps the accessible autocomplete's own announcements.**
claims.note: The extract records what is not announced (claims ruling-sam-2026-11-09-p1-008 and -009) and that the component's own announcements stand (-007), but no claim records the component decision itself: main's accessible autocomplete stays and the prototype's hand-built search is not carried over. This is the decision that makes the dropped criteria safe to drop, so reconcile needs it when it judges whether anything is left to build on the origin pages.

sources.role: the decision on what the address book stores for an address's type and uses (EUDPA-711): "use" is renamed "role" everywhere, in the record, the API, the code, the copy keys, the tests and the spec, and an address holds the roles it can play on a notification, being place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and branch address. The address book stores roles only and requires at least one; it does not store an address type and ignores one a client sends, the address type being the INS front door's grouping of roles worked out from them. The grouping of roles into sending, receiving and branch is the address book's internal rule rather than part of its API, and it refuses roles from more than one group, and a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom. The list takes role, repeatable and any-of, and searchRole, in place of addressType, use and searchUse. A role a new notification type needs is added in code, each role in exactly one group. Addresses saved before the change are not migrated: after release the addresses collection is dropped in dev and test with CDP tooling and the address book restarted, and locally the stack is restarted. The address book's list and every address picker keep pagination even though the Design Release 2.1 prototype has none, the list API paging with page and pageSize of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, because organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses; no requirement to list an organisation's addresses unpaginated is built, which ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 later reads the other way for req-611 and so outranks on that point alone.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

sources.role: the owner's decisions, as narrowed by ruling:sam-2026-10-09: on look and feel the prototype wins by default over what the real services do today; only a DR1 judgement on the same difference, or a real constraint the prototype cannot express (persistence, validation, authentication, cross-service behaviour), overrides it. The prototype never decides architecture.

claims.statement: Wherever a real service differs from Design Release 2.1 of the GB notification service prototype, the real service changes to match Design Release 2.1.
claims.quote: Goal: wherever the real services differ from Design Release 2.1, they change to match it.
claims.note: New: answers no earlier report question.

claims.statement: Which repos change (frontends, backends and other repos) is worked out from the evidence, not fixed in advance.
claims.quote: Work out from the evidence which frontends, backends and other repos that touches.
claims.note: New. The 'not fixed in advance' reading follows from 'work out from the evidence'.

claims.statement: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements.
claims.quote: The DR1 parity backlog. [...] It is not a source of requirements.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Nothing is built because the DR1 parity backlog says so on its own; this follows from the backlog not being a source of requirements and being usable only where the real frontend and the prototype clash.
claims.ref: ruling-sam-2026-10-07.md lines 7-8 (DR1 paragraph); claim 3 second sentence
claims.quote: It is not a source of requirements. Use it only when the real frontend and the prototype clash
claims.note: New. The main session's claim 3 states this in so many words; the quote implies it.

claims.statement: The DR1 parity backlog is used only where the real frontend and the prototype clash.
claims.quote: Use it only when the real frontend and the prototype clash
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Where DR1 already made a judgement on that same difference between the real frontend and the prototype, the DR1 judgement is followed.
claims.quote: if DR1 already made a judgement on that difference, follow it and cite the row.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Where a DR1 judgement is followed, the DR1 parity backlog row it comes from is cited.
claims.quote: follow it and cite the row.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The prototype (Design Release 2.1) wins by default over what the real services do today.
claims.quote: Precedence: the prototype wins by default.
claims.note: New. 'Over what the real services do today' is the main session's framing; it follows from the Goal paragraph.

claims.statement: A DR1 judgement on the same difference overrides the prototype default.
claims.quote: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. 'On the same difference' comes from the DR1 paragraph (lines 8-9).

claims.statement: A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype default; the ruling names persistence, validation, authentication and cross-service behaviour as such constraints.
claims.quote: a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. The quote says 'auth'; claim 6 reads it as authentication. Claim 6 adds 'such as', making the list examples; the quote's parenthesis can be read either as examples or as the full list.

claims.statement: Nothing other than a DR1 judgement on the same difference or a real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides the prototype.
claims.quote: Only a DR1 judgement or a real constraint the prototype can't express (persistence, validation, auth, cross-service behaviour) overrides it.
claims.note: New. In particular, what a real service does today is not on its own a reason to depart from the prototype.

claims.statement: Questions for people are kept to a minimum.
claims.quote: Decisions: keep questions for people to a minimum.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: A question for people is raised only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the prototype default nor a DR1 judgement settles it.
claims.quote: Raise one only when a difference is truly exceptional and neither the default nor DR1 settles it.
claims.note: New. Both conditions must hold. 'The default' is read as the prototype-wins default from the Precedence paragraph.

claims.statement: Increments are grouped into themes, and the themes are drawn from the evidence.
claims.quote: Themes: group the increments into themes based on the evidence.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Each theme's boundary is set by the code it touches.
claims.quote: Draw the boundaries by the code each one touches
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: Themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without pull requests that conflict with each other.
claims.quote: so themes can be built in parallel on separate machines without conflicting PRs.
claims.note: New.

claims.statement: The ruling's DR1 paragraph has an elision marked [...]: what the omitted words said about the DR1 parity backlog is not recorded.
The ruling does not say what makes a difference 'truly exceptional', so when a question for people is warranted is left open.

The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

claims.statement: Every request into the set enters the set's context before authentication runs, and every route is wrapped so it runs in that context.
claims.note: mechanism: carries the ambient set id through a request so set-keyed stores (dispatch index, journey flow, obligations, records, session) resolve to this set.

claims.statement: The entry guard runs before every handler in the set and, when it names a target, redirects there and stops the request.
The set refuses to mount when it has left any required seam unconfigured, naming each one.
The set refuses to mount when any of its journey cookies was not registered on the server.
Boot refuses an obligation model that carries any display key, such as a label, title or hint: display wording may not live in the obligation model.
Boot refuses the set when two pages both claim to collect the same obligation, naming the obligation and both pages.
Boot refuses the set when any obligation that is not system-populated is collected by no page, naming each uncovered obligation.
An obligation id may not contain a path metacharacter ('.', '[' or ']'), and boot refuses one that does.
claims.quote:
const ID_UNSAFE = /[.[\]]/
...
      throw new Error(
        `Obligation id "${obligation.name}" (at ${templatePath}) contains a path ` +
          `metacharacter ('.', '[' or ']') — ids must be path-safe`
      )

claims.statement: Boot also refuses the set when a feature's fulfilment bindings do not cover every obligation, and when a party binding is not scalar.
claims.quote:
assertObligationPurity()

claims.statement: A row with nothing in scope reads not applicable; a row with no mandatory part reads optional while untouched, then fulfilled or in progress; and a row with mandatory parts reads fulfilled when each is satisfied, in progress when something is started, and not started otherwise.

The region-of-origin code is always in scope, and it switches from optional to mandatory when the trader answers yes to whether a region code is required; the reason given is that a region code is required.
claims.note: This is the only gate in the set that keeps an obligation in scope on both branches, so the answer is never purged when the requirement flips to no.

claims.statement: The arrival date at the port is always asked and always mandatory.
The port of entry is always asked and always mandatory.
The transporter type is always asked and always mandatory.
The commercial transporter record is asked, and mandatory, only when the transporter type is Commercial, and a stored commercial transporter is dropped when the type is switched away from Commercial.
The private transporter record is asked, and mandatory, only when the transporter type is Private, and goes out of scope otherwise.
The commercial and private transporter records are mutually exclusive: only one of the two can be in scope for any transporter type.
claims.quote: // Transporter type + mutually-exclusive address blocks

claims.statement: The means of transport is always asked and always mandatory.
The transport identification is always asked and always mandatory.
The transport document reference is always asked and always mandatory.

The countries transited are asked of rail and road consignments only, and even then they are never compulsory: a trader who passes through nowhere they can name leaves the list empty, the row reads Optional and submission is not held up.
claims.note: An existing ruling: the comment records it as a design release 1 decision.

claims.statement: A conditional obligation whose in-scope decision names no mandate is treated as mandatory, so an optional conditional answer must say 'optional' outright.
claims.quote:
// `status` must say 'optional' outright — `effectiveStatus` falls back to
// 'mandatory' for an implication that carries none.

claims.statement: The place of origin is always asked and always mandatory, and is stored as one composite address record.
The consignor is always asked and always mandatory.
The consignee is always asked and always mandatory.
The importer is always asked and always mandatory.
The place of destination is always asked and always mandatory.
The reason for import is always asked and always mandatory.
The purpose in the internal market is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is internalMarket, and any stored purpose is dropped when the reason changes.
The destination country is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is transit or transhipmentOrOnwardTravel, and is otherwise out of scope and purged.
claims.note: An existing ruling: the code records the V4 data dictionary (Confluence page 6497338582) as the authority for this rule.

claims.statement: The port of exit is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is transit or temporaryAdmissionHorses, and is chosen from the same port list as the port of entry.
The exit date is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is temporaryAdmissionHorses, and is otherwise out of scope and purged.
The contact address is always asked and always mandatory.
The internal reference number is trader-entered, always in scope and always optional.
What the animals are certified for is asked once for the whole notification and is always mandatory, although the spec notes APHA may make it depend on the commodity later.
The notification's approved reference number is assigned by the system when the notification is created and is never entered by a trader; it is mandatory but no page asks for it.
The notification's reference number is shaped GBN-AG-YY-XXXXXX, where the six-character body uses Crockford base32 (0-9 and A-Z without I, L, O or U).
A notification must hold at least one commodity line, and an empty list is refused under the code obligation.commodityLine.atLeastOne.
claims.note: The commodity lines group states no upper limit on the number of lines.

claims.statement: Every commodity line must carry a commodity code.
Every commodity line must carry a species Latin name.
A commodity line's species common name is optional.
Every commodity line must carry a number of animals.
A line's number of packages is asked only when that line's commodity code is in the package-count list, and even then it is optional.
The county parish holding number is asked, and mandatory, when any commodity line's code is in the CPH-required list, and is out of scope otherwise.
Whether the consignment contains unweaned animals is asked once for the whole notification, and only when any commodity line's code is in the unweaned list.

Each animal identifier record inside a commodity line must carry at least one of seven identifiers: a microchip, a passport, a tattoo, an ear tag, a horse name, identification details or a description; an empty record is refused under obligation.unitRecord.identifiersRequired.

The at-least-one-identifier floor is stood down unless more than one commodity line has a code in the identified list, so a consignment with a single identified line is not held to it at the collection level.
claims.quote:
floorAppliesToParent: moreThanOne(
      allowListed(commodityCode, identifiedCommodityCodes, null)
    )
---
 * The inner gate names the entries that would be asked; this wrapper stands
 * the whole rule down unless there are at least two of them, and otherwise
 * hands back the inner decision untouched with the same `fulfilmentIndexes`.
claims.note: mechanism: works on the commodity-lines collection. moreThanOne returns the inner allowListed decision only when it admits more than one entry, and otherwise reports out of scope.

claims.statement: A microchip is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the microchip list, and is optional there.
A passport is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the passport list, and is optional there.
A tattoo is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the tattoo list, and is optional there.
An ear tag is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the ear-tag list, and is optional there.
A horse name is asked of an animal only when its line's commodity code and species Latin name together are in the horse-name list, and is optional there.

export const horseName = {

  within: unitRecord,
  status: 'optional',
  applyTo: allowListedPairs(

    speciesLatinName,
    horseNameCodeSpecies,
    unitRecord,

claims.statement: Identification details are asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is outside the identified list, and are optional there.
A free-text description is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is outside the identified list, and is optional there.
A permanent address is asked of an animal, and is mandatory, when its line's commodity code and species pair is in the permanent-address list.

claims.statement: A trader can attach between zero and fifteen accompanying documents to a notification, and a sixteenth is refused under obligation.accompanyingDocument.tooMany.
The fifteen-document cap is enforced on the stored notification as well as on the page's Add affordance, so a saved notification holding more than the cap is still caught afterwards.
Each accompanying document must carry its own type, attachment type, reference and date of issue; all four are mandatory within a document.
A document's upload id and filename are optional, so a document can be recorded without a file attached.
The V4 data dictionary page still reads as if a notification can hold at most one accompanying document, and the obligation model is treated as the authority until that page is amended.
claims.note: An existing ruling recorded in code: a known disagreement with the V4 source, resolved in favour of the model.

claims.statement: Each document's instance id is a session-scoped counter value such as doc1 or doc2.
claims.quote: // Instance ids are session-scoped counter values (`doc1`, `doc2`, …).

claims.statement: A gate that reads one stored answer and swaps the mandate keeps the answer in scope on both branches, while one that swaps in scope drops the stored answer when the gate answer flips.
claims.quote:
Both
 * `whenTrue` and `whenFalse` are returned verbatim, so a caller who
 * passes two in-scope decisions gets a pure status flip (e.g.
 * `regionCode` mandatory ↔ optional), and one in-scope + one
 * out-of-scope gets a purge-on-flip (e.g. `purposeInInternalMarket`
 * dropped when `reasonForImport` changes).

claims.statement: A per-line or per-animal gate decides entry by entry, so one commodity line can be asked for an identifier while another in the same consignment is not.
claims.quote:
/**
 * allowListed — in scope on entries where `gateObligation`'s stored
 * value is in the allowlist.
 *
 * - Depth-1 (gate + gated at the same identity level): pass `null` for
 *   `gatedParentGroup`; fulfilmentIndexes are the passing gate keys.
 * - Depth-N > 1 (gate broader than gated): pass the gated obligation's
 *   parent group as `gatedParentGroup`; fulfilmentIndexes are that
 *   group's fulfilmentIndexes whose ancestor prefix has a passing gate.

claims.statement: An answer that is blank never counts as outside an allowlist, so a commodity line with no code yet is not treated as an unidentified species.
claims.quote:
/**
 * notInUnionOf — dual of `allowListed`. In scope on entries whose
 * `gateObligation` stored value is not blank and not in the union of the
 * given allowlists. The union is derived at call-time and exposed on
 * `.metadata.values`.

The species check asks the reference data service for POST /commodities/species-check with the commodity lines in the body.

A species-check reply that carries no unlisted list is treated as a failure rather than as 'nothing unlisted'.

When the service is run in stub mode both the commodity search and the species check are answered from the service's own fixtures instead of reference data, and stub mode is never honoured in production.
A reference data failure is turned into a 503 'Reference data unavailable' naming the dataset that failed, either 'commodities' or 'species'.
Every call to reference data carries the service's trace headers and a JSON content type, and any non-OK reply is raised as a failure carrying the status, status text and URL.

Six commodity codes carry per-animal identifiers: cattle 0102 (ear tag, passport, tattoo), horses 0101 (microchip, passport and a horse name for Equus cabalus), swine 0103 (ear tag, tattoo), sheep 010410 (ear tag), goats 010420 (ear tag) and other live mammals 01061900 (microchip, passport, tattoo).
Those same six codes are the identified list, so a commodity line with any other code is treated as unidentified and asked for identification details and a description instead.

claims.statement: Four commodity codes carry a description: 0101 'Live horses, asses, mules and hinnies', 0102 'Live bovine animals', 01061900 'Other live animals' and 0301 'Live fish'.
Three commodity codes carry a short name: 0101 'Horse', 0102 'Cattle' and 0301 'Fish'.

claims.statement: The per-identifier code lists are derived from the one identifier table rather than written out, so a code that carries an identifier is always in that identifier's list.

claims.statement: A commodity search in stub mode matches a group when the term is a prefix of its CN code, and otherwise matches a species when every word of the term is a prefix of consecutive words of its Latin or common name.
claims.note: mechanism: the stub's own matching over the captured commodity fixtures; an empty term matches nothing by name, and a code prefix match returns the group's whole species list.

claims.statement: Stub search results are paged by slicing the flattened matches and then regrouping them by code, so a group can be split across two pages and the total counts species rather than groups.
claims.note: mechanism: paging over the stub's flattened code-and-species matches.

claims.statement: In stub mode a commodity line counts as unlisted when the captured fixtures hold no group with that code carrying that exact Latin name.

const listedInStub = ({ code, latinName }) =>
  COMMODITY_GROUPS.some(
    (group) =>
      group.code === code &&
      group.species.some((species) => species.latinName === latinName)
  )

export const unlistedLinesInStub = (lines) =>
  lines.filter((line) => !listedInStub(line))

claims.statement: Four answers decide which conditional questions a trader sees, and they are exercised as a cross product of 48 states: whether a region code is required, the reason for import (unanswered, internal market, transit or temporary admission of horses), the means of transport (unanswered or road vehicle) and the transporter type (unanswered, commercial or private).

/**
 * The scope-determining flags whose cross-product spans the conditional
 * obligations moving into and out of scope: the region-code requirement, the
 * import reason, the means of transport and the transporter type. The reason
 * axis carries transit and temporary-admission values so the reason-gated
 * destinationCountry / portOfExit / exitDate obligations are exercised.
 * 2×4×2×3 = 48 states.
 *
 * @returns {Array<object>} 48 partial answer states.
 */

claims.statement: The journey's reachability is proved over 240 answer states, each of the five seed variants overlaid with each of the 48 scope states, with unanswered values left out rather than stored blank.

claims.statement: Pressing 'Start a new notification' POSTs to /live-animals/notifications, which creates the notification, mints its GBN-AG reference and redirects straight to that notification's origin page.
claims.quote: POST | http://localhost:3000/live-animals/notifications | 302 | /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-K677Q7/origin

claims.statement: The notification reference has the shape GBN-AG-<two-digit year>-<six characters>; every reference observed in this part is GBN-AG-26 followed by six upper-case letters or digits, and the tests pin the six characters to a Crockford-style alphabet that leaves out I, L, O and U.
claims.ref: reference-strip.spec.ts line 3; trace animals-e2e-features-refer-1d81b action call@494
claims.quote: const GBN_REFERENCE = /GBN-AG-\d{2}-[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{6}/;
claims.note: notification-view-states.spec.ts uses a looser pattern /GBN-AG-\d{2}-[0-9A-Z]{6}/. Observed references: GBN-AG-26-CENMX7, -H3B3YD, -K677Q7, -Q4G1HN, -944DQK, -N31Y08, -1H9M7K, -F9ASG4, -P7M7MP, -WH70BP, -RC1HAY, -HJWS6Y, -DRKSYZ, -50HP39, -KESFE9, -5YMSDA, -FEXYBP.

claims.statement: The reference is part of every journey URL: /live-animals/notifications/<reference>/<page>, so it is already in the entry page's own URL when the user lands on it.

claims.statement: The dashboard (caption Dashboard, heading Import notification service) introduces the service and offers a Start a new notification start button.
claims.quote: Use this service to tell the authorities about live animals you are importing. You will answer a short set of questions about the consignment, then submit your notification. Start a new notification

claims.statement: The dashboard lists Your notifications with a Keyword or reference filter, a Sort by select (Arrival newest/oldest, Date created newest/oldest) with Update sort, 25 results a page and a Next pagination link.

(caption About the consignment) has an inset note that each health certificate needs a separate notification, a Search for a commodity field with a Search button, a Help with commodity codes details, and species checkboxes grouped under the matching commodity.

The journey uses GOV.UK Frontend throughout, plus MOJ date pickers, accessible-autocomplete selects and several app-specific classes (app-journey-strip, app-commodity-total, app-task-list, app-link-button, app-form-inline, notification-list).
claims.quote: moj-datepicker; data-module=app-accessible-autocomplete; app-commodity-total; app-task-list; app-link-button; notification-list__card-row
claims.note: app-commodity-total is a bespoke counter tile; app-link-button styles submit buttons as links for POST-only actions (Amend, Copy as new, Create a new notification).
